summary: Shard transponders go silent without the blockade ships moving, while Thunderbreak commander Deka keeps Fleet identifiers and Gravefire's defensive civilian overlap active.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tactical
dialogueInline.text: Shard transponders are going dark. The hulls haven't moved.

dialogueInline.speaker: Deka
dialogueInline.text: Keep ours identified. Civilian pilots need to know where we are.

dialogueInline.speaker: Deka
dialogueInline.text: Hold it open for the skiffs. Their captain keeps the lead.

panelPlan: Shard hulls keep their real positions while electronic identification beacons vanish from the Fleet tactical picture.
On Thunderbreak's established repaired command deck, Deka holds Fleet identification and authorized civilian-defense assignments rather than hiding the cruiser.
An exterior view shows independent Fleet and Gravefire coverage intersecting around the skiffs without physically joining ships or transferring authority.
directionInline: Deka remains Thunderbreak's acting commander since Issue 2. Tess commands Gravefire and requests overlap by ordinary communications. Fleet defensive shields and reciprocal-field navigation are separate real systems.
No invented Venn reinstatement or remote direction by a Shard captain.

summary: Tess commands Gravefire as she brings medical freight and skiffs to the second opening, requesting a measured shield overlap from Thunderbreak commander Deka.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tess
dialogueInline.text: Thunderbreak, Gravefire. Medical holds and skiffs in my wake. Request the overlap.

dialogueInline.speaker: Deka
dialogueInline.text: Extending sixty klicks on your side. The Gate lane is yours.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tess
dialogueInline.text: I'll keep the skiffs inside it.

panelPlan: Gravefire lifts from Shard docking access with medical freight and independent civilian skiffs in its wake; the port radiator remains damaged.
Tess calls Thunderbreak from Gravefire's own working bridge. Deka acknowledges from the Fleet cruiser's command deck without lending Tess its controls or authority.
A coherent exterior view shows limited defensive shield overlap around separate civilian hulls before they enter reciprocal-field transit.
directionInline: Tess is physically aboard Gravefire, Deka aboard Thunderbreak. Each captain retains command and the local geometry remains coherent.
The defensive overlap does not create the reciprocal-field transit window. No Venn temporary commission exists.

summary: Thunderbreak commander Deka rejects inaccurate Fleet credit for seven independent Shard captains' decision as both convoys dock; the food freighter's damaged mast remains visible.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tactical
dialogueInline.text: Both crossings clear. The food freighter needs a hull team. No weapons fire.

dialogueInline.speaker: Deka
dialogueInline.text: Identify the seven Shard ships that moved.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tactical
dialogueInline.text: The public Fleet report says our escort broke the line.

dialogueInline.speaker: Deka
dialogueInline.text: Our shields held. Their captains opened it.

panelPlan: The two convoys approach Auric separately, keeping the food freighter's bent navigation mast and the independent medical-freight geometry visible.
On Thunderbreak's working bridge Tactical reviews seven Shard hull tracks beside an exaggerated Fleet report. Deka recognizes the difference between protection and the Shards' independent act.
Deka corrects the operational record without claiming command over Shard captains or changing their faction status.
Auric dock workers begin unloading medicine and food amid the continuing shortages, not a victory parade.
directionInline: Deka still commands the repaired cruiser. She neither reinstates Venn nor becomes a spokesperson for the Verge or Shards.
Preserve supply and ship damage and the real distinction between shielding and a politically independent decision by Shard captains.
